existential_catastrophic.label: Existential & catastrophic risk
existential_catastrophic.definition: Frames AI governance around severe, irreversible, or civilization-scale harms such as CBRN proliferation, mass-casualty cyberattacks, uncontrollable autonomous AI, or extreme systemic loss of human control.
existential_catastrophic.include_when: The text explicitly cites catastrophic misuse (CBRN, mass cyber/bio harm), autonomous self-replication, loss of human control, or extreme systemic societal-scale accidents as a reason for rules.
existential_catastrophic.exclude_when: Do not assign for ordinary consumer bugs, routine privacy breaches, algorithmic bias, or standard operational software reliability issues.

national_security.label: National security
national_security.definition: Frames AI governance around defense readiness, intelligence advantage, geopolitical/strategic rivalry, foreign-adversary threats, export or compute sovereignty, or critical national-defense resilience.
national_security.include_when: The document explicitly invokes military/defense capability, intelligence, adversary competition, strategic sovereignty, or national-security critical infrastructure protection.
national_security.exclude_when: Do not assign for purely commercial growth, domestic productivity, or trade competitiveness without explicit security, defense, adversary, or strategic-sovereignty language.

economic_competitiveness.label: Economic competitiveness
economic_competitiveness.definition: Frames AI governance around macroeconomic growth, national productivity, global market leadership, industrial strength, trade/export advantage, or preventing domestic firms from falling behind foreign peers.
economic_competitiveness.include_when: The text justifies policy through GDP growth, industrial competitiveness, global AI leadership, market expansion, or strategic commercial positioning.
economic_competitiveness.exclude_when: Do not assign for worker displacement, job protection, or workforce reskilling/retraining rationales (use labor_transition), nor for generic friction-reduction/sandbox language without competitive positioning (use innovation_enablement).

fundamental_rights.label: Fundamental rights
fundamental_rights.definition: Frames AI governance around protecting human dignity, constitutional or civil rights, personal-data privacy, non-discrimination, fairness, due process, freedom of expression, democratic values, or the rule of law.
fundamental_rights.include_when: The text anchors intervention in individual rights, privacy/data-protection rights, equality/anti-discrimination, human dignity, procedural fairness, or democratic freedoms.
fundamental_rights.exclude_when: Do not assign when harm prevention is strictly framed around physical product safety, market defects, or financial fraud without rights, privacy, equality, or dignity language (use consumer_public_safety).

social_stability.label: Social stability & public order
social_stability.definition: Frames AI governance around public order, collective harmony, socialist core values, public-opinion ecosystem governance, disinformation/rumor containment, cultural/moral norms, or societal cohesion.
social_stability.include_when: The text cites public order, social harmony, ideological/value alignment, information-ecosystem stability, rumor/disinformation containment, or collective social trust.
social_stability.exclude_when: Do not assign for individual constitutional rights claims (use fundamental_rights) or narrow defective-product / individual consumer-protection rules (use consumer_public_safety).

innovation_enablement.label: Innovation enablement
innovation_enablement.definition: Frames AI governance around accelerating beneficial AI R&D, keeping rules proportional or agile, lowering compliance friction, fostering trustworthy adoption ecosystems, regulatory sandboxes, or public/private utilization.
innovation_enablement.include_when: The text argues that proportional governance, clear standards, sandboxes, or voluntary guidance are needed to unlock safe AI experimentation, deployment, and public/private adoption.
innovation_enablement.exclude_when: Do not assign when the dominant rationale is zero-sum international economic rivalry or market leadership (use economic_competitiveness).

consumer_public_safety.label: Consumer & public safety
consumer_public_safety.definition: Frames AI governance around protecting consumers, patients, children, or bystanders from physical injury, medical error, financial fraud, deceptive practices, unsafe products, or operational system harms.
consumer_public_safety.include_when: The text centers on preventing tangible harm to end users, patients, minors, or the public via product safety, clinical reliability, fraud/deception prevention, or operational risk mitigation.
consumer_public_safety.exclude_when: Do not assign when the rationale is primarily constitutional/human rights or privacy rights (use fundamental_rights) or collective public order (use social_stability).

labor_transition.label: Labor & workforce transition
labor_transition.definition: Frames AI governance around workforce disruption, job displacement, worker protections, workforce reskilling/upskilling, collective bargaining, or equitable adjustment of labor markets to automation.
labor_transition.include_when: The text explicitly cites employment disruption, worker retraining/reskilling, labor-market adjustment, workplace rights, or equitable distribution of automation gains as a reason for policy.
labor_transition.exclude_when: Do not assign merely because employment/HR appears in a list of high-risk application domains without explicit workforce-transition or reskilling rationale.

risk_assessment.label: Risk assessment
risk_assessment.definition: Systematic identification, analysis, impact assessment, or tier classification of AI risks (including fundamental-rights, privacy, or high-impact system assessments).
risk_assessment.include_when: The text requires or recommends documented risk management processes, risk classification, or algorithmic/fundamental-rights/privacy impact assessments.
risk_assessment.exclude_when: Do not conflate with empirical pre-release benchmarking (pre_deployment_testing) or adversarial attack probing (red_teaming).

pre_deployment_testing.label: Pre-deployment testing
pre_deployment_testing.definition: Empirical functional validation, accuracy/robustness benchmarking, conformity testing, or performance verification conducted prior to release or substantial modification.
pre_deployment_testing.include_when: The text explicitly expects empirical model/system testing, validation, or conformity verification before placing on the market or deploying.
pre_deployment_testing.exclude_when: Do not assign for administrative high-impact applicability self-checks or paper-only risk checklists (use risk_assessment), nor for specialized adversarial attack simulation (use red_teaming).

red_teaming.label: Red-teaming
red_teaming.definition: Structured adversarial testing, penetration testing, jailbreak/misuse probing, or simulated hostile-actor evaluation designed to elicit harmful or prohibited AI behavior.
red_teaming.include_when: The text explicitly calls for adversarial testing, red-teaming, misuse stress-testing, or hostile-input probing.
red_teaming.exclude_when: Do not assign for routine functional QA, accuracy validation, or standard software testing without an adversarial element (use pre_deployment_testing).

incident_reporting.label: Incident reporting
incident_reporting.definition: Mandatory or recommended notification of serious AI malfunctions, safety/security breaches, rights infringements, or post-market adverse events to authorities or affected users.
incident_reporting.include_when: The text specifies reporting duties triggered by serious incidents, safety failures, cyber breaches, or real-world harms.
incident_reporting.exclude_when: Do not assign for routine periodic compliance filings or initial registration notices unrelated to incidents or failures.

transparency_disclosure.label: Transparency & disclosure
transparency_disclosure.definition: Outward-facing notice to users, affected persons, or the public that they are interacting with AI, how automated decisions work, known limitations, or available opt-outs/recourse.
transparency_disclosure.include_when: The text mandates or recommends user-facing AI interaction notices, explainability disclosures to affected individuals, or public usage notices.
transparency_disclosure.exclude_when: Do not conflate with internal/regulator technical dossiers (model_documentation) or artifact-level synthetic watermarking/metadata (content_provenance).

model_documentation.label: Model documentation
model_documentation.definition: Creation and retention of structured technical documentation, model cards, system cards, compliance logs, design specifications, or downstream integrator instructions.
model_documentation.include_when: The text requires or recommends maintaining technical dossiers, model/system cards, audit logs, or downstream technical documentation.
model_documentation.exclude_when: Do not assign for brief end-user UI notices (use transparency_disclosure).

third_party_audit.label: Third-party audit
third_party_audit.definition: Independent external audit, notified-body conformity assessment, accredited certification, or external verification performed by an entity independent of the provider/deployer.
third_party_audit.include_when: The text specifies assessment, certification, or auditing by an independent external auditor, notified body, or accredited third party.
third_party_audit.exclude_when: Do not assign for purely internal self-assessments or internal compliance reviews (use risk_assessment).

access_controls.label: Access controls
access_controls.definition: Cybersecurity safeguards, authentication, role-based access, model-weight security, API gating, rate-limiting, or input/data security protecting AI assets.
access_controls.include_when: The text specifies security controls over model weights, APIs, training environments, authentication, or restricted access to sensitive capabilities/data.
access_controls.exclude_when: Do not conflate with autonomous-agent tool-permission scoping or execution kill-switches (use agentic_autonomy_controls).

compute_governance.label: Compute governance
compute_governance.definition: Obligations triggered by training-compute thresholds (e.g., FLOPs thresholds such as 10^25 FLOPs), compute-cluster reporting, cloud/chip KYC, or compute-resource oversight.
compute_governance.include_when: The text sets quantitative compute/FLOP thresholds, requires reporting large training runs, or imposes oversight on cloud/compute providers.
compute_governance.exclude_when: Do not assign for general industrial investment or national datacenter buildout plans lacking operational compute oversight controls.

content_provenance.label: Content provenance
content_provenance.definition: Explicit or implicit marking, watermarking, cryptographic provenance metadata (e.g., C2PA), or machine-readable labeling of AI-generated or synthetically altered media.
content_provenance.include_when: The text requires or recommends visible labels, invisible watermarks, or metadata provenance embedded in synthetic text, audio, image, or video outputs.
content_provenance.exclude_when: Do not assign for generic chatbot interaction banners or algorithmic-decision explanations that do not mark synthetic outputs (use transparency_disclosure).

human_oversight.label: Human oversight
human_oversight.definition: Operational human-in-the-loop or human-on-the-loop review, manual override/stop controls, meaningful human appeal/intervention, or limits on solely automated consequential decisions.
human_oversight.include_when: The text establishes concrete duties for human supervision, override/intervention capability, or human review of automated decisions.
human_oversight.exclude_when: Do not assign for purely rhetorical slogans such as 'human-centric AI' or 'serving humanity' without operational human-control expectations.

registration_licensing.label: Registration or licensing
registration_licensing.definition: Prior registration in a public or regulatory AI/algorithm registry, pre-market filing, conformity declaration filing, or formal permit/license to deploy or operate.
registration_licensing.include_when: The text requires operators/providers to register models, algorithms, or high-risk systems with an authority or obtain a license/filing approval.
registration_licensing.exclude_when: Do not conflate with offshore legal representative appointment (use domestic_representative) or enforcement sanction authority (pair with licensing_requirement under enforcement_mechanisms).

agentic_autonomy_controls.label: Agentic autonomy controls
agentic_autonomy_controls.definition: Operational safeguards for autonomous or tool-using AI agents: unique agent identity/attribution, least-privilege tool/API permissions, action scoping, credential revocation, default-deny execution, or emergency kill-switches.
agentic_autonomy_controls.include_when: The text explicitly governs multi-step autonomous agents, tool/API invocation permissions, delegated identity, or agent execution interruptibility.
agentic_autonomy_controls.exclude_when: Do not assign for static Q&A chatbots or single-turn generative models without autonomous action/tool execution.

training_data_governance.label: Training data governance
training_data_governance.definition: Operative obligations on training/fine-tuning datasets: lawful provenance and licensing checks, copyright opt-out compliance, dataset bias/quality curation, training personal-data minimization, or public training-content summaries.
training_data_governance.include_when: The text sets concrete rules governing collection, curation, lawful provenance, copyright compliance, or disclosure of AI training/fine-tuning datasets.
training_data_governance.exclude_when: Do not assign for generic runtime user-privacy notices unrelated to model training or fine-tuning data.

frontier_safety_evaluation.label: Frontier safety evaluation
frontier_safety_evaluation.definition: Structured frontier-model or systemic-risk capability evaluations targeting severe harms (CBRN, offensive cyber, autonomous replication, loss of control), including pre-release government or AISI evaluation access.
frontier_safety_evaluation.include_when: The text requires or establishes frontier/systemic capability evaluations or government/AI Safety Institute pre-release model evaluations.
frontier_safety_evaluation.exclude_when: Do not assign for routine narrow-sector product QA or medical-device clinical accuracy trials (use pre_deployment_testing).

open_weight_obligations.label: Open-weight obligations
open_weight_obligations.definition: Explicit legal obligations, conditional exemptions, or systemic-risk overrides governing open-source or open-weight AI model releases and downstream modification.
open_weight_obligations.include_when: The text explicitly defines duties, exemptions, or carve-out conditions for open-weight or open-source AI models.
open_weight_obligations.exclude_when: Do not assign when the document never distinguishes open-weight/open-source releases from proprietary deployments.

domestic_representative.label: Domestic representative
domestic_representative.definition: Requirement for foreign or offshore AI providers lacking a local establishment to designate an authorized domestic legal representative or point of contact inside the jurisdiction.
domestic_representative.include_when: The text mandates that extraterritorial/foreign AI providers appoint a local authorized representative or domestic legal agent.
domestic_representative.exclude_when: Do not assign for general domestic company registration or internal Chief AI Officer appointments.

mandatory.label: Mandatory
mandatory.definition: Unconditional binding duty expressed with compulsory legal language ('shall', 'must', 'is required to', '하여야 한다', '应当', 'なければならない').
mandatory.include_when: The operative clause imposes an unqualified compulsory requirement on covered entities.
mandatory.exclude_when: Do not assign when the duty is triggered only by specific thresholds/exceptions (use conditional) or phrased as 'should'/'endeavour to' (use recommended/aspirational).

conditional.label: Conditional
conditional.definition: Binding or operational duty triggered only when specified thresholds, risk tiers, procurement contexts, or opt-in safe harbors apply ('where high-risk', 'if compute exceeds...', 'as a condition of...').
conditional.include_when: The obligation applies strictly upon meeting explicit scope triggers, thresholds, or opt-in conditions stated in the text.
conditional.exclude_when: Do not assign for universal unconditional mandates (use mandatory) or purely non-binding suggestions (use recommended).

recommended.label: Recommended
recommended.definition: Actionable non-binding expectation, best practice, or soft-law guidance ('should', 'is encouraged to', 'is expected to', '할 수 있다/권고한다', '望ましい', '鼓励').
recommended.include_when: The text prescribes concrete operational practices through guidance, standards, or 'should'/'endeavour to' phrasing without legal compulsion.
recommended.exclude_when: Do not assign for legally binding mandates (use mandatory) or high-level policy slogans lacking operational steps (use aspirational).

aspirational.label: Aspirational
aspirational.definition: High-level principle, strategic goal, or future policy intent ('strive to promote', 'aims to foster', 'will explore') without concrete operational compliance steps.
aspirational.include_when: The text expresses broad normative vision, long-term strategic ambition, or exploratory intent rather than actionable compliance duties.
aspirational.exclude_when: Do not assign when the document specifies concrete operational controls or actionable checklists (use recommended, conditional, or mandatory).

civil_penalty.label: Civil penalties
civil_penalty.definition: Administrative fines, statutory monetary penalties, civil damages, or turnover-based financial sanctions.
civil_penalty.include_when: The text explicitly authorizes monetary fines, administrative penalties, or statutory civil liability damages.
civil_penalty.exclude_when: Do not assign for criminal imprisonment/prosecution (use criminal_penalty) or unpenalized corrective notices (use regulatory_supervision).

criminal_penalty.label: Criminal penalties
criminal_penalty.definition: Imprisonment, criminal fines, or referral for criminal prosecution under penal statutes.
criminal_penalty.include_when: The text explicitly specifies criminal offenses, custodial sentences, or referral to criminal law/prosecutors.
criminal_penalty.exclude_when: Do not assign for purely administrative or civil monetary fines (use civil_penalty).

market_access_restriction.label: Market-access restrictions
market_access_restriction.definition: Product bans, market withdrawal or recall orders, service suspension, app-store takedowns, or prohibitions on placing non-compliant systems on the market.
market_access_restriction.include_when: The text authorizes prohibiting, suspending, withdrawing, recalling, or blocking market availability of an AI system/service.
market_access_restriction.exclude_when: Do not assign for routine pre-market license issuance/revocation alone (use licensing_requirement) unless market withdrawal/ban powers are stated.

procurement_condition.label: Procurement conditions
procurement_condition.definition: Compliance clauses tied to government purchasing, public-sector contracting, or federal/ministerial funding eligibility.
procurement_condition.include_when: The text conditions government acquisition, vendor contracts, or public funding on meeting AI governance requirements.
procurement_condition.exclude_when: Do not assign for general private-sector regulation unrelated to public procurement or funding.

licensing_requirement.label: Licensing requirements
licensing_requirement.definition: Regulatory authority to condition lawful operation on prior licensing, pre-market approval, or algorithm filing, including suspension or revocation of authorization.
licensing_requirement.include_when: The text grants authorities power to withhold, condition, suspend, or revoke a mandatory operating license or pre-market approval.
licensing_requirement.exclude_when: Do not assign for purely voluntary certification schemes (use soft_enforcement).

regulatory_supervision.label: Regulatory supervision
regulatory_supervision.definition: Investigatory powers, inspections, information/document demands, corrective orders, cease-and-desist notices, or ongoing supervisory oversight by an authority.
regulatory_supervision.include_when: The text empowers a regulator or ministry to inspect, investigate, request records, or issue corrective/compliance orders.
regulatory_supervision.exclude_when: Do not assign when the issuer only publishes non-binding voluntary advice without supervisory authority (use soft_enforcement).

reporting_obligation.label: Reporting obligations
reporting_obligation.definition: Enforceable statutory or administrative duty to submit compliance reports, impact assessments, filings, or disclosures to a government authority.
reporting_obligation.include_when: The text obligates covered entities to submit filings, assessments, or compliance reports to an authority as an oversight hook.
reporting_obligation.exclude_when: Do not assign for voluntary self-disclosure pledges lacking an official submission channel (use soft_enforcement).

soft_enforcement.label: Soft enforcement
soft_enforcement.definition: Voluntary adherence, best-practice recommendations, self-regulation, public naming/guidance persuasion, or safe-harbor incentives lacking direct coercive sanctions.
soft_enforcement.include_when: The text relies on voluntary adoption, non-binding guidance, codes of practice, or reputational/safe-harbor incentives.
soft_enforcement.exclude_when: Do not assign as the sole mechanism when the document establishes binding statutory fines or coercive orders.

none_specified.label: No explicit enforcement
none_specified.definition: The document articulates no enforcement, compliance, or oversight mechanism whatsoever.
none_specified.include_when: The text is a pure vision statement, R&D roadmap, or administrative notice containing zero compliance or enforcement hooks.
none_specified.exclude_when: Do not co-assign alongside active enforcement mechanisms unless the text explicitly carves out unenforceable sections.

binding_law.label: Binding law
binding_law.definition: Enacted primary statute, EU Regulation, presidential enforcement decree, or formally promulgated administrative regulation carrying direct legal obligations and enforceable remedies.
binding_law.include_when: The document itself is enacted legislation or a binding statutory regulation/decree in force or formally promulgated.
binding_law.exclude_when: Never assign to FAQs, Q&As, press releases, overview slides, or un-enacted draft notices even if they describe a binding law.

executive_action.label: Executive action
executive_action.definition: Presidential executive order, binding OMB directive to federal agencies, or cabinet-level executive order binding government bodies.
executive_action.include_when: The document is a formal head-of-state, presidential, cabinet, or OMB directive binding executive agencies.
executive_action.exclude_when: Do not assign to parliamentary statutes (use binding_law) or non-binding ministry white papers (use strategy_statement).

regulatory_guidance.label: Regulatory guidance
regulatory_guidance.definition: Interpretive or supervisory guidance from a regulator or ministry carrying administrative compliance weight, safe-harbor presumption, or enforcement signaling.
regulatory_guidance.include_when: The document is official regulator/ministry guidance interpreting legal duties or outlining supervisory expectations.
regulatory_guidance.exclude_when: Do not assign to formally enacted statutory decrees (use binding_law) or technical metrology standards (use standards_guideline).

standards_guideline.label: Standards guideline
standards_guideline.definition: Technical framework, evaluation guide, risk-management profile, or voluntary national standard (e.g., NIST RMF, TC260/GB/T, J-AISI guides) without direct legal compulsion unless incorporated by reference.
standards_guideline.include_when: The document is issued by a standards body, AISI, or technical ministry as a technical assurance framework or guideline.
standards_guideline.exclude_when: Do not assign to signatory political pledges or codes of practice (use voluntary_commitment).

voluntary_commitment.label: Voluntary commitment
voluntary_commitment.definition: Formal signatory pledge, code of practice, or multilateral voluntary code of conduct where adherence is opt-in.
voluntary_commitment.include_when: The document is a formal pledge, pact, or signatory code of practice/conduct (e.g., EU AI Pact, EU GPAI Code of Practice, Hiroshima Code).
voluntary_commitment.exclude_when: Do not assign to non-signatory technical standards (use standards_guideline) or unilateral government strategies (use strategy_statement).

strategy_statement.label: Strategy statement
strategy_statement.definition: Aspirational national AI plan, policy vision, action plan, or research report containing no operative legal or technical compliance duties.
strategy_statement.include_when: The document sets broad national policy priorities, R&D goals, or strategic agendas without operative regulatory mandates.
strategy_statement.exclude_when: Do not assign to legally binding directives (use executive_action or binding_law).

primary_instrument.label: Primary instrument
primary_instrument.definition: Canonical, distinct primary text of a law, executive action, substantive regulatory guideline, technical standard, national strategy, or major voluntary framework. Default population for headline divergence metrics.
primary_instrument.include_when: The document is the authoritative primary text of a distinct governance instrument.
primary_instrument.exclude_when: Exclude FAQs, Q&As, press releases, overview slides, bilingual duplicates, consultation drafts, and superseded versions.

companion_resource.label: Companion resource
companion_resource.definition: Official supplementary material tied to a primary instrument: FAQs, Q&As, expert interpretations, press announcements, transmittal memos, templates, portal overview pages, crosswalks, or translation mirrors.
companion_resource.include_when: The artifact explains, summarizes, translates, or accompanies a distinct primary instrument.
companion_resource.exclude_when: Do not assign to standalone primary statutes, guidelines, or technical frameworks.

draft_consultation.label: Draft / consultation
draft_consultation.definition: Public consultation draft, legislative notice, or superseded pre-adoption draft version retained for provenance and drafting history.
draft_consultation.include_when: The document is a draft bill, notice for public comment, or pre-final draft.
draft_consultation.exclude_when: Exclude adopted or active primary instruments (use primary_instrument).

historical_baseline.label: Historical baseline
historical_baseline.definition: Superseded or revoked official instrument retained explicitly for longitudinal policy–framing drift analysis.
historical_baseline.include_when: The document was once an authoritative primary instrument but has been formally superseded or revoked.
historical_baseline.exclude_when: Exclude currently active instruments (use primary_instrument) and un-adopted drafts (use draft_consultation).

draft.label: Draft
draft.definition: Published for public comment, expert review, or legislative deliberation; not yet formally adopted.
draft.include_when: The text is explicitly marked as a draft, proposal, or consultation notice without formal enactment.
draft.exclude_when: Once superseded by an adopted final version, transition to superseded.

adopted_not_yet_effective.label: Adopted (pending)
adopted_not_yet_effective.definition: Formally enacted or promulgated instrument whose statutory effective date lies in the future.
adopted_not_yet_effective.include_when: The law or rule is officially adopted/promulgated with a future effective_date.
adopted_not_yet_effective.exclude_when: Transition to active once effective_date has passed.

active.label: Active
active.definition: Currently in legal force or actively maintained official government policy/guidance.
active.include_when: The instrument's effective date has passed (or it applies immediately upon publication) and it has not been repealed or superseded.
active.exclude_when: Do not assign to pending future-effective statutes (use adopted_not_yet_effective), un-enacted drafts (use draft), or replaced texts (use superseded).

superseded.label: Superseded
superseded.definition: Formally replaced, repealed, revoked, or succeeded by a newer official version (chained via supersedes_id on the replacement document).
superseded.include_when: A newer enacted law, executive order, plan, or version has officially replaced or revoked this document.
superseded.exclude_when: Do not assign to instruments that remain concurrently valid alongside newer sectoral guidance.
